meta.title: US Accounting Account Master (Principles of Accounting I)
meta.basis: Standard US GAAP intro textbook chart of accounts for a small corporation with perpetual inventory
meta.note: Contra accounts keep their parent type and say contra in desc. Freight-In is theory-only; entries debit Merchandise Inventory.

accounts.name: Cash
accounts.desc: Money the company can spend right away. It includes coins, paper money, and checks received.
accounts.ex: Sold merchandise for cash → Dr Cash / Cr Sales Revenue

accounts.name: Petty Cash
accounts.desc: A small fund kept on hand for minor payments like postage or snacks.
accounts.ex: Set up a petty cash fund of $200 → Dr Petty Cash / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Accounts Receivable
accounts.clue: Customers owe the company, no note
accounts.desc: Money customers owe the company for goods or services sold on credit.
accounts.ex: Sold merchandise on account → Dr Accounts Receivable / Cr Sales Revenue

accounts.name: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
accounts.desc: A contra asset that reduces receivables by the amount you expect not to collect.
accounts.ex: Estimated bad debts → Dr Bad Debt Expense / Cr Allowance for Doubtful Accounts

accounts.name: Notes Receivable
accounts.desc: A written promise from someone to pay the company a set amount later, usually with interest.
accounts.ex: Accepted a 90-day note from a customer → Dr Notes Receivable / Cr Accounts Receivable

accounts.name: Interest Receivable
accounts.desc: Interest the company has earned but not yet been paid.
accounts.ex: Accrued interest earned on a note → Dr Interest Receivable / Cr Interest Revenue

accounts.name: Rent Receivable
accounts.desc: Rent the company has earned from a tenant but not yet collected.
accounts.ex: Accrued rent earned → Dr Rent Receivable / Cr Rent Revenue

accounts.name: Merchandise Inventory
accounts.desc: Goods the company bought to resell to customers. It is an asset until the goods are sold.
accounts.ex: Purchased merchandise on account → Dr Merchandise Inventory / Cr Accounts Payable

accounts.name: Supplies
accounts.desc: Items like paper and pens that the company has bought but not yet used up.
accounts.ex: Purchased supplies for cash → Dr Supplies / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Prepaid Insurance
accounts.desc: Insurance paid for in advance. It becomes an expense as the coverage period passes.
accounts.ex: Paid a one-year premium → Dr Prepaid Insurance / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Prepaid Rent
accounts.desc: Rent paid before the period it covers. It becomes an expense as time passes.
accounts.ex: Paid three months' rent in advance → Dr Prepaid Rent / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Prepaid Advertising
accounts.desc: Advertising paid for before the ads run. It becomes an expense once the ads appear.
accounts.ex: Paid for a future ad campaign → Dr Prepaid Advertising / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Land
accounts.desc: The land the company owns for its operations. It is not depreciated.
accounts.ex: Purchased land for cash → Dr Land / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Buildings
accounts.desc: Structures the company owns and uses, like an office or a warehouse. They are depreciated over time.
accounts.ex: Purchased a building with a bank loan → Dr Buildings / Cr Bank Loan Payable

accounts.name: Equipment
accounts.desc: Long-lived machines and tools used in the business. They are depreciated over their useful lives.
accounts.ex: Purchased equipment for cash → Dr Equipment / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Vehicles
accounts.desc: Cars and trucks the company owns and uses. They are depreciated over time.
accounts.ex: Purchased a delivery truck for cash → Dr Vehicles / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Furniture
accounts.desc: Desks, chairs, and shelving used in the business. They are depreciated over time.
accounts.ex: Purchased office furniture on account → Dr Furniture / Cr Accounts Payable

accounts.name: Accumulated Depreciation—Buildings
accounts.desc: A contra asset that holds all depreciation recorded so far on buildings.
accounts.ex: Recorded building depreciation → Dr Depreciation Expense / Cr Accumulated Depreciation—Buildings

accounts.name: Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment
accounts.desc: A contra asset that holds all depreciation recorded so far on equipment.
accounts.ex: Recorded equipment depreciation → Dr Depreciation Expense / Cr Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment

accounts.name: Accumulated Depreciation—Vehicles
accounts.desc: A contra asset that holds all depreciation recorded so far on vehicles.
accounts.ex: Recorded vehicle depreciation → Dr Depreciation Expense / Cr Accumulated Depreciation—Vehicles

accounts.name: Accumulated Depreciation—Furniture
accounts.desc: A contra asset that holds all depreciation recorded so far on furniture.
accounts.ex: Recorded furniture depreciation → Dr Depreciation Expense / Cr Accumulated Depreciation—Furniture

accounts.name: Advances to Employees
accounts.desc: Money the company lends or pays ahead to employees. The employee owes it back.
accounts.ex: Advanced $300 to an employee → Dr Advances to Employees / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Deposits Paid
accounts.desc: Money the company paid as a deposit and expects to get back, like a security deposit.
accounts.ex: Paid a refundable security deposit → Dr Deposits Paid / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Accounts Payable
accounts.desc: Money the company owes suppliers for goods or services bought on credit.
accounts.ex: Purchased merchandise on account → Dr Merchandise Inventory / Cr Accounts Payable

accounts.name: Notes Payable
accounts.desc: A written promise by the company to pay a set amount later, usually with interest.
accounts.ex: Signed a 60-day note to a supplier → Dr Accounts Payable / Cr Notes Payable

accounts.name: Interest Payable
accounts.desc: Interest the company has incurred but not yet paid.
accounts.ex: Accrued interest on a note → Dr Interest Expense / Cr Interest Payable

accounts.name: Salaries Payable
accounts.desc: Salaries employees have earned that the company has not yet paid.
accounts.ex: Accrued salaries at year-end → Dr Salaries Expense / Cr Salaries Payable

accounts.name: Wages Payable
accounts.desc: Hourly wages employees have earned that the company has not yet paid.
accounts.ex: Accrued wages at period end → Dr Wages Expense / Cr Wages Payable

accounts.name: Unearned Revenue
accounts.desc: Cash received before the company delivers the service or goods. The company owes the work.
accounts.ex: Received cash for services not yet done → Dr Cash / Cr Unearned Revenue

accounts.name: Unearned Rent
accounts.desc: Rent received in advance from a tenant for a future period.
accounts.ex: Received six months' rent in advance → Dr Cash / Cr Unearned Rent

accounts.name: Sales Tax Payable
accounts.desc: U.S. sales tax collected from customers that the company must pass on to the state.
accounts.ex: Sold merchandise for cash plus 6% tax → Dr Cash / Cr Sales Revenue, Cr Sales Tax Payable

accounts.name: Income Taxes Payable
accounts.desc: Income taxes the company has recorded but not yet paid to the government.
accounts.ex: Recorded income tax owed → Dr Income Tax Expense / Cr Income Taxes Payable

accounts.name: FICA Taxes Payable
accounts.desc: U.S. Social Security and Medicare taxes withheld from pay, plus the company's share, not yet paid.
accounts.ex: Recorded employer payroll taxes → Dr Payroll Tax Expense / Cr FICA Taxes Payable

accounts.name: Federal Income Taxes Payable
accounts.desc: Federal income tax taken out of employees' pay that the company must send to the IRS.
accounts.ex: Recorded payroll with income tax withheld → Dr Salaries Expense / Cr Federal Income Taxes Payable and Cash

accounts.name: Utilities Payable
accounts.desc: Utility bills for services already used but not yet paid.
accounts.ex: Accrued the electric bill → Dr Utilities Expense / Cr Utilities Payable

accounts.name: Dividends Payable
accounts.desc: Dividends the board has declared but the company has not yet paid to shareholders.
accounts.ex: Declared a $2,000 dividend → Dr Dividends / Cr Dividends Payable

accounts.name: Customer Deposits
accounts.desc: Money customers paid ahead as a deposit. The company owes goods, service, or a refund.
accounts.ex: Received a deposit on a special order → Dr Cash / Cr Customer Deposits

accounts.name: Bank Loan Payable
accounts.desc: The amount the company has borrowed from a bank and must repay.
accounts.ex: Borrowed $20,000 from First Valley Bank → Dr Cash / Cr Bank Loan Payable

accounts.name: Common Stock
accounts.desc: The amount shareholders paid in when they bought the company's shares.
accounts.ex: Issued shares for cash → Dr Cash / Cr Common Stock

accounts.name: Retained Earnings
accounts.desc: Net income earned over time, minus dividends, that the company has kept in the business.
accounts.ex: Closed net income → Dr Income Summary / Cr Retained Earnings

accounts.name: Dividends
accounts.desc: A contra equity account for distributions to shareholders. It reduces equity and is not an expense.
accounts.ex: Declared a cash dividend → Dr Dividends / Cr Dividends Payable

accounts.name: Sales Revenue
accounts.desc: Income earned from selling merchandise to customers.
accounts.ex: Sold merchandise for cash → Dr Cash / Cr Sales Revenue

accounts.name: Sales Returns and Allowances
accounts.desc: A contra revenue account for goods customers send back or price cuts for flawed goods.
accounts.ex: Customer returned goods → Dr Sales Returns and Allowances / Cr Accounts Receivable

accounts.name: Sales Discounts
accounts.desc: A contra revenue account for discounts given to customers who pay early.
accounts.ex: Collected within the discount period → Dr Cash, Dr Sales Discounts / Cr Accounts Receivable

accounts.name: Service Revenue
accounts.desc: Income earned by performing services for customers.
accounts.ex: Performed services for cash → Dr Cash / Cr Service Revenue

accounts.name: Fees Earned
accounts.desc: Income earned by charging fees for professional or advisory work.
accounts.ex: Earned consulting fees on account → Dr Accounts Receivable / Cr Fees Earned

accounts.name: Interest Revenue
accounts.desc: Interest the company earns on notes or bank balances.
accounts.ex: Received interest on a note → Dr Cash / Cr Interest Revenue

accounts.name: Rent Revenue
accounts.desc: Income earned by renting property to others.
accounts.ex: Received rent from a tenant → Dr Cash / Cr Rent Revenue

accounts.name: Commission Revenue
accounts.desc: Income earned for selling or arranging sales on behalf of others.
accounts.ex: Earned a sales commission in cash → Dr Cash / Cr Commission Revenue

accounts.name: Gain on Sale of Equipment
accounts.desc: The amount received above the book value when equipment is sold.
accounts.ex: Sold equipment above book value → Dr Cash, Dr Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment / Cr Equipment, Cr Gain on Sale of Equipment

accounts.name: Miscellaneous Revenue
accounts.desc: Small bits of income that do not fit any other revenue account.
accounts.ex: Sold scrap paper for cash → Dr Cash / Cr Miscellaneous Revenue

accounts.name: Cost of Goods Sold
accounts.desc: The cost of the merchandise the company sold during the period.
accounts.ex: Recorded the cost of goods sold → Dr Cost of Goods Sold / Cr Merchandise Inventory

accounts.name: Salaries Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of salaries earned by employees during the period.
accounts.ex: Paid salaries → Dr Salaries Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Wages Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of hourly wages earned by employees during the period.
accounts.ex: Paid wages → Dr Wages Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Payroll Tax Expense
accounts.desc: The employer's share of U.S. payroll taxes, such as FICA, on employee pay.
accounts.ex: Recorded the employer's FICA → Dr Payroll Tax Expense / Cr FICA Taxes Payable

accounts.name: Rent Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of renting space used in the business.
accounts.ex: Paid monthly rent → Dr Rent Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Utilities Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of electricity, gas, and water used in the business.
accounts.ex: Paid the electric bill → Dr Utilities Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Insurance Expense
accounts.desc: The part of insurance cost that applies to the current period.
accounts.ex: Recorded insurance used up → Dr Insurance Expense / Cr Prepaid Insurance

accounts.name: Supplies Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of supplies the company used during the period.
accounts.ex: Recorded supplies used → Dr Supplies Expense / Cr Supplies

accounts.name: Advertising Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of ads and other promotion during the period.
accounts.ex: Paid for a radio ad → Dr Advertising Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Depreciation Expense
accounts.desc: The part of a long-lived asset's cost assigned to the current period.
accounts.ex: Recorded depreciation → Dr Depreciation Expense / Cr Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment

accounts.name: Bad Debt Expense
accounts.desc: The estimated cost of customer balances the company will not collect.
accounts.ex: Estimated uncollectible accounts → Dr Bad Debt Expense / Cr Allowance for Doubtful Accounts

accounts.name: Interest Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of borrowing money during the period.
accounts.ex: Paid interest on a loan → Dr Interest Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Telephone Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of phone service used in the business.
accounts.ex: Paid the phone bill → Dr Telephone Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Internet Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of internet service used in the business.
accounts.ex: Paid the internet bill → Dr Internet Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Travel Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of airfare, lodging, and other travel for business.
accounts.ex: Paid for a business trip → Dr Travel Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Delivery Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of delivering goods to customers.
accounts.ex: Paid for delivery of goods sold → Dr Delivery Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Repairs and Maintenance Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of routine repairs and upkeep that keep assets working.
accounts.ex: Paid to repair a machine → Dr Repairs and Maintenance Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Office Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of everyday office needs that do not fit another expense account.
accounts.ex: Paid for office cleaning → Dr Office Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Bank Service Charges
accounts.desc: Fees charged by the bank for account services.
accounts.ex: Bank charged a monthly fee → Dr Bank Service Charges / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Postage Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of stamps and shipping mail.
accounts.ex: Bought stamps for cash → Dr Postage Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Training Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of training courses for employees.
accounts.ex: Paid for a staff workshop → Dr Training Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Entertainment Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of entertaining clients or customers.
accounts.ex: Paid for a client dinner → Dr Entertainment Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Donations Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of gifts the company gives to charities.
accounts.ex: Donated $500 to a local charity → Dr Donations Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Property Tax Expense
accounts.desc: The cost of property taxes on land and buildings the company owns.
accounts.ex: Paid property tax → Dr Property Tax Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Income Tax Expense
accounts.desc: The income tax cost recorded for the period.
accounts.ex: Recorded income tax → Dr Income Tax Expense / Cr Income Taxes Payable

accounts.name: Loss on Sale of Equipment
accounts.desc: The shortfall when equipment is sold for less than its book value.
accounts.ex: Sold equipment below book value → Dr Cash, Dr Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment, Dr Loss on Sale of Equipment / Cr Equipment

accounts.name: Loss from Theft
accounts.desc: The cost of assets or goods lost to theft.
accounts.ex: Inventory was stolen → Dr Loss from Theft / Cr Merchandise Inventory

accounts.name: Miscellaneous Expense
accounts.desc: Small costs that do not fit any other expense account.
accounts.ex: Paid a small odd cost → Dr Miscellaneous Expense / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Freight-In
accounts.desc: The cost of shipping purchased goods to the company. Under perpetual inventory it goes to Merchandise Inventory.
accounts.ex: Paid freight on goods bought (perpetual) → Dr Merchandise Inventory / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Cash Over and Short
accounts.desc: Holds small differences between the cash counted and the cash records. A shortage is a debit; an overage is a credit.
accounts.ex: Drawer was $5 short → Dr Cash Over and Short / Cr Cash

accounts.name: Income Summary
accounts.desc: A temporary account used at year-end to gather revenues and expenses before closing to Retained Earnings.
accounts.ex: Closed revenue to the summary → Dr Sales Revenue / Cr Income Summary
